newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's Cavallo launches bid for Congress.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's Cavallo launches bid for Congress.

text.p: Domingo Cavallo, a former Argentine economy minister, on Wednesday launched his candidacy for a congressional seat in October midterm elections and admitted his sights were set on the presidency.

"I won't hide the fact I want to govern the republic, and therefore I will run for president in 1999 or 2003," Cavallo said on announcing his congressional bid during a rally of the neo-liberal party Action for the Republic.
"I'm leaving behind my profession and vision as an economist, because I gave it all I've got and I'm very happy to have done so," Cavallo said.

"But I think I've got something else to offer my country...which is the experience I've gathered through my thoughts, studies, reflections, dialogue, contact with reality -- undertaken not with intellectual aims but rather as a form of action to resolve problems," he said.

Launched in 1991, Cavallo's convertibility program pegging the value of the peso to the U.S. dollar and his free-market policies tamed Argentina's runaway inflation and led to four years of strong economic growth.

But the outspoken minister was dismissed last July by President Carlos Menem after clashes with leaders of the old guard of the ruling Peronist party over his accusations of corruption and government-linked "mafias."
Argentina elects half of its 257-seat chamber of deputies in October.

Cavallo will head the Action for the Republic's list of deputies in the federal capital, while the party's slate in Buenos Aires province will be headed by former Radical party economist Adolfo Sturtzenegger.
